target_reference_entry:
[23] C. Wang, L. Xie, Y. Lin, W. Wang, Y. Chen, Y. Bu, K. Zhang, S. Lu, Thru-the-wall 
eavesdropping on loudspeakers via RFID by capturing sub-mm level vibration, Proc. 
ACM Interact., Mob., Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 5 (4) (2021) 1–25.
paper_level_summary_zh: 该论文在相关工作部分将目标论文归类为利用RFID进行语音窃听的典型工作，明确提及了其通过捕获亚毫米级振动的穿墙窃听能力。正文未对目标论文进行方法使用、性能比较或限制反馈，属于普通相关文献引用。

evidences.evidence_quote: Wang et al. [23] extended RFID sensing to enable through-wall eavesdropping.
evidences.evidence_context: TagMic [22], built with COTS devices, was the first to show RFID tags could be used for eavesdropping. Wang et al. [23] extended RFID sensing to enable through-wall eavesdropping. RF-Mic [20] uses RFID tags to create a low-cost, hidden, and flexible voice monitoring system, marking an early application of RFID in voice surveillance.

evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 正文仅将[23]列为语音窃听领域的一项扩展工作，描述为'enable through-wall eavesdropping'，属于普通相关文献列举，未详细描述其方法或能力，因此为ordinary_reference。
